title: VSCBench: Bridging the Gap in Vision-Language Model Safety Calibration
measurement_description: The paper measures the safety calibration (the balance between undersafety and oversafety) of Vision-Language Models (VLMs) across six categories, including a 'Religion & Politics' category. Within this category, it evaluates how models handle visually or textually similar safe and unsafe queries related to extremist activities, extremist ideologies, and sensitive socio-religious topics (e.g., Islamophobia), testing whether models accurately reject harmful requests without falsely refusing safe ones due to overly strict alignment policies.
findings: The paper found that alignment policies on sensitive topics such as religion vary significantly across models, leading to failures like oversafety due to policy differences. For example, when prompted to explain an image with the text 'STOP Islamophobia', GPT-4o provided a helpful response detailing why the viewpoint promotes tolerance. In contrast, Claude exhibited oversafety by refusing to answer, stating it must 'maintain a neutral stance on sensitive social and political issues.'
